draft.note_text:
Subjective: 37F with hx of HTN and DM presents with headache. Gets occasional headaches but they have been getting worse lately. Home BP checked about once a week and higher than usual for the past 3 weeks: 160/87, most recent 175/92. On lisinopril 20 mg daily; admits missed doses, mainly on weekends when busy. Headache 7/10 at onset, pounding; Tylenol brings it down to 4-5/10 for a while, then it recurs through the day. No prior headaches like this. Hx of migraine about once every 1-2 years, takes nothing for it. Denies congestion, cough, runny nose; feels this is different from her seasonal allergies. Home blood sugar around 120, sometimes down to 100. No increased urination. Walks for exercise.
Objective: BP at last visit 124/82 per chart review. Exam: no frontal sinus tenderness, no maxillary sinus tenderness, no lymphadenopathy (pt reported slight tenderness on tapping forehead, less over cheekbones, and slight tenderness on neck palpation).
Assessment: 1. Headache. 2. HTN, elevated home readings with missed lisinopril doses. 3. DM, blood sugar running a little high per clinician.
Plan: Continue Tylenol for headache. Increase lisinopril from 20 mg to 40 mg once daily for HTN and headaches. Continue home BP checks. Blood work ordered including HbA1c. Diabetic education provided for review. OK to continue walking; exercise encouraged. Follow up in clinic with this clinician or Dr. Ruth after labs are done to recheck BP control.
